extracted.intended_audience: authors and teams conducting systematic reviews and meta-analyses (health researchers, review authors, journal editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting standards and methodological guidance for planning, conducting, and reporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses, with emphasis on transparency (PICOS, protocol, search, selection, extraction, bias assessment, and synthesis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives (Item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an explicit statement of the questions being addressed, and the rationale for them, stated precisely and explicitly so readers can understand the review’s scope and applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good review questions may be narrowly focused or broad. Precisely stated objectives help define eligibility criteria and search strategy. Frame questions using the PICOS components (population, interventions/exposure, comparators, outcomes, study designs) to improve explicitness. Examples illustrate how to state the review aim (e.g., target population, interventions compared, outcomes measured, and design limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: PICOS components (part of Item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly define the five PICOS components: (P) patient population or disease, (I) interventions/exposures, (C) comparators, (O) main outcomes/endpoints of interest, and (S) study designs chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PICOS to frame the review question and improve explicitness; specify each component clearly. The choice between narrow and broad questions affects applicability and enables detection of bias and sensitivity analyses. See Box 2 for more detail (not included here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol and Registration (Item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if a review protocol exists, where it can be accessed (e.g., web address), and provide registration information including registration number if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A protocol pre-specifies objectives and methods (outcomes of interest, data extraction methods, synthesis plans) and reduces biased post hoc decisions (e.g., selective outcome reporting). Authors may modify protocols but should describe modifications and their rationale, since changes (especially to primary outcomes) can affect bias. Registration can reduce duplication and increase transparency; report collaborators' endorsement for individual patient-data meta-analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility Criteria (Item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify study characteristics and report characteristics used as eligibility criteria, giving rationale (e.g., years considered, language, publication status; PICOS; minimum follow-up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly defined eligibility criteria inform search strategy and ensure studies are selected systematically and without bias. Distinguish study eligibility (populations, interventions, comparators, outcomes, designs, follow-up) from report eligibility (language, publication status, inclusion of unpublished material). State exclusions (e.g., transplant patients) and whether studies lacking specific outcomes will be excluded, since this affects potential selective reporting bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Sources (Item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe all information sources used in the search (e.g., databases with dates of coverage), contact with study authors, and date last searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each database report the database name, platform/provider (Ovid, Dialog, PubMed), and start/end dates to let readers assess currency and facilitate updates. Report who developed/conducted the search. Describe supplementary approaches (handsearching journals, checking references, trial registries, regulatory sites, contacting authors/manufacturers) and any attempts to obtain missing information from investigators or sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy reporting (Item 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the full electronic search strategy for at least one major database, including any limits used, such that it could be repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide in-text examples or appendix strategy (search lines, terms, boolean combinations). If multiple searches were needed for different parts of the question, provide at least one strategy for each part. State whether search strategies were peer reviewed. If journal space is limited, provide strategies as web extras or appendices and archive searches for reproducibility and updates. Report search constraints (time, resources, indexing limitations, language/date restrictions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Selection (Item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the process for selecting studies: screening, determining eligibility, inclusion in the review, and if applicable, inclusion in meta-analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how records were screened (title/abstract), how often full texts were needed, and any exclusions of record types. Use the PRISMA flow diagram to summarize the process. Describe who performed each stage, whether multiple reviewers screened independently, how disagreements were resolved (consensus, arbitration), and report inter-rater agreement where relevant. Use at least two investigators for difficult selection judgments to reduce erroneous exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection process (Item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods of data extraction from reports (e.g., piloted forms, independently by two reviewers) and processes for obtaining and confirming data from investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report development and piloting of extraction forms, who extracted what data, whether extractions were duplicated and done independently, and how disagreements were resolved. Describe attempts to contact study authors for missing or unclear information, success in obtaining additional data, and whether individual patient data were sought. Describe steps to avoid double counting across multiple reports of the same study and algorithms for selecting data from overlapping reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of study reports and data extraction transparency (Box 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report detailed counts and processes from identified records to included studies (distinguish reports vs studies), and describe the steps in screening, full-text retrieval, and eligibility application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use text plus PRISMA flow diagram to show numbers at each stage (identified records; potentially relevant studies; included studies), and ideally by outcome. Describe promotion criteria (yes/no/maybe), who participated in each step, and any calibration or training exercises. Report whether all reports of a study were considered and steps taken to reconcile inconsistencies across reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data items (Item 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: List and define all variables for which data were sought (e.g., PICOS elements, funding sources), and any assumptions and simplifications made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify characteristics extracted (participant demographics, intervention details, outcomes, follow-up length, inclusion/exclusion criteria). Report variables sought even if not obtained, and refer to protocol and archived extraction forms. Describe any variables added after starting the review and reasons. State assumptions made for missing or unclear information and justify them (exercise caution with qualitative information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias in individual studies (Item 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods used for assessing risk of bias in individual studies (specify whether at study or outcome level or both) and how this information will be used in data synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a component/domain-based approach over scales that produce numeric summary scores. Specify which methodological components were assessed (e.g., sequence generation, allocation concealment, blinding, incomplete outcome data, selective outcome reporting, other bias). Report who assessed bias, whether assessments were blind, if they were done by multiple reviewers independently, any calibration exercises, and how bias assessments informed inclusion/exclusion, sensitivity analyses, subgroup analyses, or quantitative synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cochrane risk of bias tool components (Box 4 examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key empirically supported domains that influence bias in randomized trials: sequence generation, allocation concealment, blinding, incomplete outcome data, selective outcome reporting, and other sources of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a component/domain approach; avoid unvalidated numeric scales. Apply additional topic- or study-specific bias items case-by-case. Explain how identified risks of bias may affect results and consider sensitivity/subgroup analyses based on these assessments. Present any algorithms used to resolve overlapping reports and logical inconsistencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary measures (Item 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the principal summary measures for each outcome (e.g., risk ratio, odds ratio, risk difference, difference in means, standardized mean difference, hazard ratio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify primary outcomes and the summary effect measure for each. Explain the choice where possible. For binary outcomes use risk ratio/odds ratio/risk difference; for continuous outcomes use difference in means or standardized difference when scales vary; for time-to-event outcomes use hazard ratios (provide log hazard ratio and SE). Note differences between measures (e.g., hazard ratio vs risk ratio) and when conversions or estimations are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned methods of analysis and data handling (Item 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods for handling data and combining results, including planned measures of consistency/inconsistency (e.g., I2) for meta-analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report data processing steps (combining groups, aligning scales, reversing signs so scales are consistent, reconstructing or imputing SDs from other statistics), and methods for time-to-event conversions. Describe statistical combination methods (fixed vs random effects), how heterogeneity will be evaluated (tests and I2 with uncertainty intervals), and planned approaches to impute missing variance or within-patient correlations when needed. State when combination is not appropriate and report planned sensitivity and subgroup analyses.
